sources.note: Own project factual-data exception. Exact missing record 1492-1650 and four MultiPolygons decoded; tests include Demak/Gowa/Kupang, early Papua, but exclude Malacca/Johor Lama/Banda Aceh/Brunei/Banten/Ternate/Tidore. No aliases. Detailed identity and point evidence saved separately.

sources.title: Great Mosque of Demak, institutional profile and architectural description
sources.note: Original mosque institution profile read directly. History and architecture sections describe tiered roof, four main posts and open veranda; community foundation/saint accounts identified as traditional. Turtle year-symbol interpreted as renovation in 1401 Saka/1479. No wooden-scrap post legend or all-original timber assertion.

sources.title: National Research and Development Centre of Archaeology, Archaeological Discoveries in Indonesia (1950-1980)
sources.note: Original institutional PDF indexed text, printed page 100, sections 3.1 and 3.2. Reproduced with exact query full PDF URL + "Tridonorejo" "100". Direct web and local fetch failed; no claim of full PDF reading. Survey finds rooftiles, kendi, bowls, beads, Chinese/Annam ceramics dated fourteenth-sixteenth centuries. Exact concluding harbor range cut off in index, so omitted.

sources.title: Nurul Adliyah Purnamasari and Saputra Andika, Jejak Kerajaan Gowa (2020)
sources.note: Balai Arkeologi Sulawesi Selatan original repository abstract read through indexed full text. Somba Opu shift, harbor and 1525 earthen palace wall; 1605 conversion of distinct Gowa/Tallo rulers. Abstract has inconsistent precise dates for conversion and 1669 capture relative to Cummings/Mostert; only conversion year used, ending instead sourced to Mostert.

sources.title: Tristan Mostert, Scramble for the spices: Makassar’s role in European and Asian competition in the Eastern Archipelago up to 1616 (2018)
sources.note: Original scholarly chapter read directly, printed pages 25-29. Gowa/Tallo federation, external diplomacy, spice competition, 1615 hostage incident and 1666-1669 defeat by VOC/local allies led by Arung Palakka. Kept separate work from Mostert’s 2015 globe chapter.

sources.title: William Cummings, The Makassar Annals (2010)
sources.note: Critical bilingual edition read directly. Printed page 42 = PDF page 53, year 1631, May rain/interest entries and September royal hall; printed page 22 dates principal witness VT 25 to 1874, page 4 identifies its serang script and warns no original seventeenth-century manuscript available. Rain variant in footnote 60 says another copy has stones. Family interpretation limited to court records, not general demographics. All quoted sample/gloss/name words combined below 25.

sources.title: Tristan Mostert, study of Pattingalloang’s globe order, in Aan de overkant (2015), pages 77-96
sources.note: Original publisher PDF indexed passages verified; direct open fails. Exact queries full URL + "globe" "Spaans" and "Pattingalloang" "1644". Printed page 82 describes requested globe exceeding 1.3m diameter and 1648 dispatch of Spanish world map, Latin four-volume atlas, burning glass and telescopes. Order originated with Pattingalloang, not a spontaneous European gift. No delivery date asserted for giant globe.

sources.title: Balai Pelestarian Cagar Budaya Banten, Sistem Pengaturan Air Bersih pada Masa Kesultanan Banten (2014)
sources.note: Original heritage agency page completely readable through exact-title indexed query; direct open fails. Tasikardi under Maulana Yusuf 1570-1580, mother’s island retreat, later family recreation; irrigation/palace water, terracotta pipes and three settling/filter stations. Source does not date each filter: public text distinguishes the accumulated system from sixteenth-century lake foundation. Banten is outside imported polygon, explicitly comparative.

sources.title: Kaoru Ueda, An Archaeological Investigation of Hybridization in Bantenese and Dutch Colonial Encounters: Food and Foodways in the Sultanate of Banten, Java, 17th-Early 19th Century, dissertation abstract
sources.note: Original Boston University two-page abstract read directly. Local cooking pots/lids, stoves, Dutch dietary shift bread to rice, male cooks and local women as wives/concubines. Broader seventeenth-early nineteenth-century study; not all finds belong before 1650. Banten outside outline.

sources.title: National Library Board Singapore, Mother Island: Finding Singapore’s Past in Pulau Lingga (2022)
sources.note: Original institutional article, A Trading Power section, indexed full paragraph checked: Melaka court fled after Portuguese invasion 1511 and re-established along Johor river. Later Riau-Lingga dual government not projected into sixteenth century. Both sites outside this particular umbrella polygon.

proposedOverrides.name: Malaysian Islamic states
proposedOverrides.summary: A broad atlas umbrella across parts of the Southeast Asian archipelago, not modern Malaysia or one Islamic state. Distinct examples from Demak and Gowa accompany clearly identified neighboring comparisons.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Standalone plural regional umbrella, no aliases
batchIdentityNotes.mapEvidence: Four MultiPolygons, world1492/world1500/world1530/world1600. Includes Demak and Gowa; reaches Kupang and initially southern New Guinea. Excludes tested Malacca, Johor Lama, Banda Aceh, Brunei, Banten, Ternate and Tidore points. Bounds and test outputs in identity.json and point-checks.json.
batchIdentityNotes.publicResolution: Overview explicitly explains huge archipelago shape and no uniform government/religion. Demak/Gowa anchor most passages; Banten food/water and Johor are explicitly beyond-outline comparisons. The 1605 Gowa court conversion demonstrates noncontemporaneous adoption; no faith assignment to New Guinea/Timor.
batchIdentityNotes.related: Malacca, Aceh and Brunei cards remain separate. Modern malaysia belongs to another date/identity. No new geographic correction or successor links proposed.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: 1631 annals text, not a surviving 1631 autograph: modern Roman transliteration from Cummings 2010, principal serang-script witness VT 25 dated 1874; variant explicitly disclosed.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: No securely local 1492-1650 household toilets or therapeutic protocol established in checked sources. Water-engineering example is neighboring Banten with mixed chronology; no fabricated healthcare or universal schooling.
